question: Does the n=53 shared-factor-log IC batch advantage survive against Kuhn-Struik batched signed-Frobenius rho, and at what batch size (if any) does IC overtake?

rho_ks.dp_bits_selection: chosen on disjoint corpus n53-ks-dp-tuning-v1 (batch_seed 777001, L=1024) by total group additions; d=2 was 2.4% fewer additions at 3.9x the memory

panel.order: block parity alternates which arm runs first

matching: every fixture's published_fixture_scalar, published_q and recovered scalar must agree between arms
primary_metric: per-block process wall ratio IC/rho (from /usr/bin/time real), median over blocks
decision_rule: IC is said to overtake at L only if all 3 block ratios at L are < 1. Mixed blocks are reported as unresolved.
prior_panel: runs/paired_L32_L1024 used producer v1 (scalar-multiplication walk starts, d=8)
host_caveat: shared host; other sessions active; load average recorded per run
